Each cap has beta(n−1,1) radial parameter and independent simplex Dirichlet factors; cap fraction η=binom(n−2,r−1)/A(n−1,r−1). For θ=1−λη>0, first-moment subtraction yields E X_i=r/n−γ(d_i−λr/n), γ=η(r−1)(n−r−1)/[θ r(n−r)]. Second moments arise by explicit cap Dirichlet moments and symmetric hypersimplex slice inclusion-exclusion. The codegree coefficient κ has nonnegative u=r−2,v=n−r−2 polynomial u²v²+3u²v+u²+3uv²+9uv+3u+v²+3v, positive except n=4,r=2 where a nonempty degree-regular two-cap configuration has θ=0. Thus regular degrees iff centered; within degree regularity codegree uniformity iff isotropy. Positive volume implies positive covariance on tangent space. Independent exact fractional check reconstructed n=6,r=3,λ=2 centroids (1/2)^6 and (73/162,1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2,89/162), and algebraically checked κ; bounded checks do not replace universal cap proof.

final_claim: For a full-dimensional rank-r sparse-paving matroid base polytope obtained by disjoint hypersimplex corner cuts, the continuous-volume centroid displacement is proportional to circuit-hyperplane degree imbalance. Exact second moments depend on degrees and pair codegrees; among one-designs isotropic covariance is equivalent to a two-design, with an Ehrhart-equivalent centroid-separation example.
limitations: Restricted to full-dimensional sparse-paving base polytopes and uniform intrinsic continuous volume; no claim for vertex-uniform covariance or unregularized isotropy converse.
